meaning:
ἀνα-κάμπτω
[in LXX: 1Ch.19:5, Jer.3:1, al. (שׁוּב), Jer.15:5 (סוּר) ;]
1. trans., to bend or turn back.
2. Intrans., to return: Mat.2:12, Act.18:21, Heb.11:15; metaphorically (cf. MM, VGT, see word), Luk.10:6.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Being warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own country another way.
If a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; but if not, it will return to you.
but taking his leave of them, he said, “I must by all means keep this coming feast in Jerusalem, but I will return again to you if God wills.” Then he set sail…
If indeed they had been thinking of that country from which they went out, they would have had enough time to return.
